Zoroastrianism. This is an ancient Persian religion founded by the prophet Zoroaster. The exact date is disputed, but scholarly estimates range from around 1500 to 500 BCE, with debate centered on the earlier date. Zoroastrianism is one of the world's oldest ethical monotheistic religions. It teaches that the universe is a cosmic struggle between Ahura Mazda, the Wise Lord or god of good, and Angra Mainyu, the Destructive Spirit or evil. This religion introduces key theological concepts later adopted by Judaism, Christianity, and Islam: eschatology, or end times, resurrection, judgment after death, heaven and hell, and the ultimate triumph of good over evil. Zoroastrianism shaped Persian imperial ideology and remains a living tradition practiced by Parsis and other communities.

The prophet Zoroaster taught that the cosmos is fundamentally ethical: a struggle between good, embodied in Ahura Mazda and his angels called the Amesha Spentas, and evil, embodied in Angra Mainyu and his demons called the daevas. Humans are moral agents who choose sides in this cosmic conflict. Ahura Mazda is the supreme god, creator of all good. Evil is co-eternal with good but will ultimately be defeated, unlike later monotheisms where God is absolutely transcendent and all-powerful.

Zoroastrianism introduced the concept of apocalypse, or afrinagan: at the end of history, Saoshyant, a savior figure born of Zoroaster's seed, will arrive. The dead will be resurrected and the world will be purified by fire and molten metal. Individual judgment after death precedes the cosmic judgment. The soul is tested and crosses the Chinvat Bridge, the bridge of separation. The righteous cross safely to paradise while the wicked fall to hell.

Good conduct follows the principle of asha, truth, righteousness, and order, against druj, lie, chaos, and disorder. Virtue consists of good thoughts, good words, and good deeds, expressed in the Zoroastrian formula: humata, hukhta, hvarshta. Fire is sacred in Zoroastrianism, symbolizing divine presence and purity. The faith included fire temples and the practice of exposing the dead, a form of sky burial, to avoid polluting earth and water.

Zoroastrianism heavily influenced later Western and Middle Eastern religions. The concepts of Satan, angels, resurrection, paradise, and apocalyptic end-times likely derive from Zoroastrian sources, making this ancient Persian faith one of the most consequential religions in human history.
